Area.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/2] The aim was to identify the psychological problems and processes leading up to, and following, suicide attempts in order to identify key opportunities for prevention. [/page/2/Text/5] Through face-to-face interviews in qualitative studies the meanings and purposes attributed to self-harm and attempted suicide by those engaging in the behaviour have been explored. The results are broadly consistent with research in the general population: self-harm and attempted suicide help prisoners to deal with feelings of anxiety, anger and helplessness. They provide relief from stressful feelings and emotions and give the prisoner control over an impersonal environment (Cullen, 1985; Jeglic, Vanderhoff, & Donovick, 2005; Loucks, 1997). [/page/3/Text/5] This allows a picture of the person's more general 'career' in relation to self-harm to be described (i.e. how many times over someone's life did they attempt suicide?
